The smooth, well-defined decline phase and the absence of the rapid fluctuations or extended plateau seen in Type II supernovae or the extreme luminosity of superluminous events further support this classification. The relatively modest peak magnitude and standard decline rate are consistent with normal Type Ia supernovae rather than peculiar subtypes like SNIa-91bg or SNIax.
